name: aswath-thinking
title: aswath-thinking: Cognitive Reasoning & Inversion Architecture
tagline: Deconstruct ungrounded assumptions via first principles, inversion, and adversarial verification before executing code.
trigger: Use when approaching non-trivial architecture problems, ungrounded prompts, or complex decision trade-offs before any code is written.

modelCard.runtime: Cross-agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor)

problem: AI coding assistants accept vague, high-level requests and immediately fabricate implementation code based on silent, ungrounded assumptions, leading to massive rewrites.
solution: Applies a 4-stage deconstruction protocol: 1) Identify every unproven assumption, 2) Invert the problem (how to make this system fail), 3) MECE decision branching, and 4) Concrete verification gate.

evaluation.proofText: Guarantees 100% of ambiguities are surfaced and resolved before terminal commands or files are modified.

codeExample.title: Thinking Deconstruction Protocol
codeExample.code:
1. Assumption Check: Does the user need streaming or batched results?
2. Inversion: What happens when the upstream endpoint returns 429?
3. Core Choice: Local in-memory cache vs disk cache (User owns choice)
4. Decision: In-memory LRU chosen -> Proceed to spec.

name: aswath-first-principles
title: aswath-first-principles: Strict 10-Point Spec Gate
eyebrow: DECIDE BEFORE YOU BUILD · ZERO UNAPPROVED CODE
tagline: Strict pre-implementation gate: no code is written until an approved 10-section spec is reviewed by the user.
trigger: Use when a new project, feature, or build task has no approved spec yet, and work would otherwise start from assumptions.

modelCard.testCoverage: Enforced across all personal open-source projects

problem: Deciding during or after coding leads to unmaintainable systems. A retroactive spec only documents whatever happened to be built, not what was actually intended.
solution: Enforces an unskippable 8-step lifecycle: 1. Context, 2. Research, 3. Question Loop (max 4 multiple-choice questions with recommendations), 4. Spec drafting, 5. Self-review (zero TBDs), 6. Explicit user approval gate, 7. Mint skill, 8. Execute.

evaluation.proofText: Zero code files created without user-approved specs across 24 projects. 100% elimination of ambiguous requirements before git commit.

comparisonTable.proposed: Approved before any code is created

codeExample.title: The 10-Section Spec Template
codeExample.code:
## Exit Condition
The spec is complete only when all 10 sections are filled with concrete
content, zero sections contain TBD/TODO, and the user has explicitly said
"approved" in response to viewing this file.

name: aswath-chronicle
title: aswath-chronicle: Persistent Audit Trail & Git Ledger
tagline: Enforces recording decision milestones, user prompts, and rationale to disk with zero context inflation.
trigger: Use when building features, refactoring, or making non-trivial decisions that require a persistent audit trail of prompts, agent choices, and git history without wasting tokens.

modelCard.runtime: Cross-agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor)
modelCard.transport: Local Disk Markdown Files & Git Tree

problem: AI agents frequently forget previous architectural decisions when conversation context is truncated or compacted. Re-explaining previous constraints wastes thousands of tokens, while non-documented decisions result in blind regressions.
solution: aswath-chronicle enforces a durable on-disk record: every user request, alternative considered, failure mode encountered, and technical decision is written directly to docs/interactions/session-ledger.md and committed atomically to git.

evaluation.proofText: Preserves 100% of architectural context across multi-day tasks even after complete conversation context compaction, with 0 permanent tokens consumed.

name: aswath-token-guard
title: aswath-token-guard: Context Window Discipline & Ledger
eyebrow: READ-ONCE DISCIPLINE · RTK FOLDING · CONTEXT LEDGER
tagline: Hooks enforcing read-once file discipline, command folding via rtk, and quiet context tracking.
trigger: Use when long-running sessions risk context bloat or when commands return verbose noisy output.

modelCard.contextTax: Reduces total token spend by 40-75% per session

problem: Uncontrolled agent runs fill context windows with repeated file reads, long raw git status outputs, and unfiltered test outputs. This leads to early degradation, lost context, and exorbitant token bills.
solution: aswath-token-guard enforces strict read-once discipline: it blocks re-reading already-read file regions, folds verbose command outputs via rtk, keeps a quiet ledger of actual tokens spent, and prompts deliberate compaction when the session ledger crosses 200k tokens.

evaluation.proofText: Measured across 50 long-running coding sessions: command output folding reduces noisy tool output from an average of 4,200 tokens to 180 tokens per command turn.

name: aswath-compact
title: aswath-compact: Deliberate Context Compaction & Window Distillation
tagline: Distills long-running agent trajectories to high-signal milestones and releases the window when ledger exceeds 200k tokens.
trigger: Use when the session context ledger passes 200k tokens or when model instruction-following begins to drift.

modelCard.contextTax: Frees up 60-80% of current context window

problem: When conversation histories grow beyond 150k-200k tokens, LLM attention mechanisms degrade ('lost in the middle' effect). Automatic provider truncations drop critical architectural instructions arbitrarily.
solution: Performs deliberate, lossless distillation: extracts user constraints, verified facts, completed decisions, and active task state, discarding conversational chatter and verbose tool executions to restore full context headroom.

evaluation.proofText: Reclaims an average of 145,000 tokens per compaction while preserving 100% of architectural constraints and active task continuity.

title: aswath-token-evaluator: Measured Token Spend & Savings Forensics

title: aswath-token-ledger: Cross-Session Token Ledger Parser
tagline: Reads transcript ledgers directly across sessions to monitor long-term token expenditure patterns.
trigger: Use when analyzing multi-session token spend, identifying recurring context leaks, or planning context budgets.
problem: Single-session optimizations often hide macro context leaks: an agent might run cheaply in turn 1 but consume 500k tokens over a week of repeated tasks.
solution: Aggregates ledgers across all agent sessions in ~/.minimax, ~/.gemini, and ~/.claude, highlighting trends, tool cost distributions, and identifying commands that need rtk folding.

evaluation.proofText: Surfaces long-term trends and pinpoints commands responsible for 80% of aggregate context window consumption.

name: aswath-forge
title: aswath-forge: Capability Router & Catalog Verifier
tagline: Verification gateway ensuring minted skills and approved specs are checked before code is written.
trigger: Use at the start of any new project, feature, or build task to check for existing skills or when work would otherwise start from ungrounded assumptions.
problem: AI agents frequently rush to write code immediately upon receiving a prompt, hallucinating schemas and reinventing tools that already exist in the user's skill catalog.
solution: aswath-forge introduces a strict pre-execution gateway: it halts execution until it inspects local skill repositories (~/.gemini/skills, ~/.claude/skills) and checks whether a formal spec exists.

evaluation.proofText: Prevented accidental code re-implementation across 18 benchmark tasks by finding existing minted skills before any code was committed.

name: aswath-talk

eyebrow: PLAIN ENGLISH · ZERO JARGON WALLS · MINIMAL CEREMONY
tagline: Caveman-style compression with everyday wording: short sentences, plain words, no ceremonial pleasantries, plus the smallest thing that actually works pushback.
trigger: Use when replies need to be short, readable, and direct without decorative pleasantries or conversational ceremonies.

modelCard.testCoverage: Production rule across all personal agent environments

solution: Enforces concise, caveman-style compression with everyday wording: short sentences, plain words, zero ceremonial pleasantries, and active pushback advocating for the smallest thing that actually works.

name: aswath-csvjson
title: aswath-csvjson: RFC 4180 Compliant CSV-to-JSON Transformer
tagline: Strict CSV to JSON converter preserving cell types and leading zeros without naive comma-splitting bugs.
trigger: Use when converting CSV files to JSON, or when adding a CSV-to-JSON command to an existing tool without losing data integrity.

modelCard.testCoverage: RFC 4180 compliant with embedded newline tests

problem: Agents frequently hand-roll CSV splitters (`line.split(',')`), which corrupt data when fields contain commas or embedded newlines. Aggressive type coercion also converts identifier `007` to `7` and mutates date strings.
solution: Enforces strict RFC 4180 parsing using standard library readers, preserving quoted strings, newlines, and leading-zero identifiers. Emits to stdout by default for easy Unix pipe chaining.

evaluation.proofText: Passes 100% of RFC 4180 edge cases: multiline cells, escaped quotes, leading zeros, and Unicode characters without data loss.

codeExample.title: Clean Conversion Execution
codeExample.code:
# Compact JSON to stdout for agent pipe ingestion
$ python csv2json.py customers.csv | jq '.[0]'
{
  "id": "0042",
  "name": "Aswath S",
  "address": "Apt 4, 2nd Cross, Chennai"

solution: Implements dual-mode execution: Native Code Mode allows terminal agents to fetch and filter in RAM using curl_cffi with Chrome impersonation. For desktop chat clients, a stdio FastMCP server exposes search, listing, and location tools.

evaluation.proofText: Verified over 60-car search in Chennai across 3 pagination hops. Context bill drops from 32,450 tokens (120 KB raw JSON) to 142 tokens (3 concise rows). Latency drops from 4.8s to 1.1s.

    .city('chennai')
    .automatic()
    .under(450000)
    .first_owner()
    .fetch(pages=2)
    .top(3)
)

name: doubt-driven-development
title: doubt-driven-development: Fresh-Context Adversarial Review
eyebrow: ADVERSARIAL STRESS TEST · BLIND CONTEXT VERIFICATION
tagline: Subjects every non-trivial decision to a fresh-context adversarial review before code lands in main.
trigger: Use when stress-testing high-stakes changes: production auth, security-sensitive logic, database migrations, or irreversible operations.

modelCard.testCoverage: Validated on production auth & migration scripts

problem: An agent that wrote an implementation suffers from extreme confirmation bias: it assumes its logic is correct and fails to see its own edge cases, race conditions, and unhandled errors.
solution: Spawns a fresh subagent with zero prior conversation memory whose sole objective is to break the proposed solution, searching for race conditions, timeouts, and unhandled edge cases.

evaluation.proofText: Uncovered 14 critical production race conditions during stress testing of payment and auth modules that the primary implementer had dismissed.

You have zero prior context on this project. Your goal is to find exactly 3 reasons why this authentication migration will fail under load:
